newsitem.title: JAPAN: G7 may not single out Japan trade--monetary source.
newsitem.headline: G7 may not single out Japan trade--monetary source.

text.p: Leaders of the Group of Seven (G7) major industrial nations may not single out Japan's trade surplus at their summit meeting in Denver, Colorado on June 20-22, an international monetary source told reporters on Monday.
The source said G7 finance ministers are expected to explain their countries' current economic conditions, including the issues of inflation, growth, external balances and the financial markets.
"Therefore, no special attention is likely to be paid to Japan's external imbalances," the source said.
The finance ministers will hold their own talks on the sidelines of the meetings of the heads of the G7 states.
Japan will refer particularly to changes in its economic structure when it discusses its trade surplus at the G7 meeting, the source said.
Japanese Finance Ministry officials have said that Tokyo's surplus in the balance of goods and services trade is unlikely to grow significantly over the medium term.
